acceptance: The Dataproc and Dataproc Serverless adapters share one implementation of the GCS upload and result-read helpers, with behaviour unchanged and the duplicate groups gone.
context: Filed 2026-11-25 from the run-timeout close-out; duplicate report read on develop f1c6343bbf. Line numbers are approximate; re-read before editing.
description:
## Problem
`make duplicate-check` on develop f1c6343bbf reports two duplicate groups (26 of the 1920 duplicated lines) between the two GCP adapters:
- `_upload_to_gcs(gcs_path, content)`: `benchbox/platforms/gcp/dataproc_adapter.py` (about lines 368-377) and `dataproc_serverless_adapter.py` (about 261-270), byte-identical: strip `gs://`, split bucket and blob, `upload_from_string`.
- `_retrieve_results(job_id | batch_id)`: same files (about 379-394 and 272-287), identical apart from the parameter name: list blobs under `{gcs_prefix}/results/<id>/` and parse every `.json` blob as JSON lines.
A fix to one (for example a `gs://` parsing or encoding bug) can miss the other. Both predate the run-timeout work; they surfaced while reducing duplication for #4507.

## Prior art
- `benchbox/platforms/gcp/_gcs_path.py` (`parse_gcs_staging_dir`, `GcsStagingPath`) is already shared GCS code imported by both adapters.
- `benchbox/platforms/base/cloud_spark/staging.py` (`CloudSparkStaging`, its S3 and GCS subclasses) already wraps a GCS client for uploads and listings.
- #4507 shared the Livy session wait the same way (`LivyStatementMixin` in `benchbox/platforms/azure/_livy_mixin.py`).
Decide extend vs new: prefer extending `_gcs_path.py` (or the GCS staging class, if it fits without widening its contract) over a new module.

## Change
Move the two helpers into one shared place, taking the storage client, bucket and prefix as arguments, and make both adapters call it. Keep the adapters' `_upload_to_gcs` / `_retrieve_results` methods only if tests or callers need those seams; otherwise update the tests (`tests/unit/platforms/gcp/test_dataproc_coverage.py`, `test_dataproc_serverless_paths.py`) to patch the shared helper.

## Decision gates
- Behaviour-preserving refactor only: same blob names, same parsing (JSON lines, skip blank lines, only `.json` blobs), same exceptions. Changing `download_as_string` (deprecated) to `download_as_bytes`, or any behaviour, is a separate change: STOP and record it rather than bundle it.
- Adapter SDK imports stay lazy: the shared code must not import `google.cloud.storage` at module import time.
- If sharing through `CloudSparkStaging` would change its public contract, use `_gcs_path.py` instead.

## Verification rubric
Pass: `make duplicate-check-delta` reports a decrease (the two GCP groups gone, 1920 -> about 1894 on today's base) and lists no gcp group; the existing GCP adapter tests pass unchanged in assertions; a new test of the shared helper covers `gs://` and bare paths, a `.json` blob with blank lines, and non-`.json` blobs ignored; `make lint-imports`, `make platform-manifest-check` and `make pr-preflight` exit 0.
Fail: any behaviour change, an eager SDK import, or a remaining GCP duplicate group.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again.
